sections.h2: Selling in the Village of Caledonia
sections.html: Caledonia is a Racine County village on the northeastern corner of the county, with an estimated 25,229 residents in July 2025. Two governments matter when you sell. The village handles assessment records and permit history, and Racine County records the deed. Whether you hire an agent, sell privately or take a direct cash offer depends mostly on the condition of the house, its location (older neighborhood or large rural lot) and your deadline.

The village stretches across roughly 45 square miles along Lake Michigan and is a collection of separate communities, among them Franksville, Husher and Tabor. A Franksville lot attracts a different buyer than a house near Douglas Avenue, so frame your price discussion around the specific setting. I-94 runs close by, Milwaukee is 18 miles north and Chicago 73 miles south, and Caledonia and DeBack Farms are the village's two business parks.

The housing stock mixes older farmhouses, long narrow lots near the shore and rural-suburban parcels. On those, buyers commonly ask about septic systems, drainage and grading.

Roughly four of every five Caledonia homes are lived in by their owners, and the median value of an owned home is $303,400. Price a worn house at that median and buyers will likely negotiate for repairs.

sections.h2: How the village assessor fits into a sale
sections.html:
Caledonia has outsourced its assessing since 1999, to Cole-Layer-Trumble at first and now Tyler Technologies. The assessor sets market-based values for taxable property. Tax rates and collection are not the assessor's job, and the village says so plainly.

  • A 2025 assessment ratio of 0.9533 was published by the village.
  • The assessor is open to the public on Thursdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with clerical staff answering questions on Monday to Wednesday mornings.
  • The assessor page carries a preliminary assessment list by address and the state's Guide for Property Owners.

The annual sequence is notices in summer, an open-book period, a deadline for giving notice of objection, then the Board of Review. If you suspect your value is too high, ask the assessor's office when the schedule is set. File an objection on form PA-115A no later than 48 hours ahead of the board's first meeting, unless the board excuses you for good cause.

Residential and commercial permits come from the village Building Department, which employs building, electrical and plumbing inspectors. The state's online system handles permits for new homes, while plumbing and electrical permits are separate from the main application.

Anything you built or replaced after buying the house should have a closed permit, because a buyer's lender or inspector may check and open work can pull an offer down. Phone the department with your parcel address and request the permit history ahead of listing.

  • Septic mound systems need a sanitary permit from Racine County Planning and Development, which can supply records for your lot.
  • Rural and lakeshore parcels can have drainage, grading and culvert certifications on file, since the village requires them for new homes.
  • Put copies of every final inspection sign-off in your sale folder.

Racine County records Caledonia deeds. A standard document costs a flat $30, plus the state transfer fee. Wis. Stat. 77.22 assigns the fee to the grantor at 30 cents for each $100 of value, and for a land contract the value counts as all the principal the buyer agrees to pay.

The state's Real Estate Transfer Return exists only online, through the Department of Revenue, and the Register of Deeds will not help you fill it in. The county directs questions to the department at (608) 264-6885 or (608) 266-1594. The county also checks each deed for these points:

  • Both grantor and grantee are named
  • The grantor's signature is notarized or authenticated
  • The legal description is complete
  • The parcel identification number appears
  • The drafter and a return address are listed
  • The page is legible and meets state margin rules

Call the Register of Deeds at (262) 636-3208 with questions. When the owner has died and the deed still names the decedent, ask whether a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest (form HT-110, $30 to record) is needed before the sale.

A completed real estate condition report must reach the buyer within 10 days after the contract is accepted, for most sellers (Wis. Stat. 709.02). Chapter 709 applies to one to four dwelling units and also to unbuilt land, which uses a separate vacant land report. Rural Caledonia parcels make that second type relevant.

A late report gives the buyer two business days after the 10 days run out to rescind and get any deposit back. Fiduciaries such as personal representatives, trustees and conservators who never occupied the property are excused. Other sellers should answer every question on the form, because a report is complete only when each item has an answer or a permitted substitute.

List when the house is up to date on repairs and you can wait on a buyer's financing. Consider cash when the house needs work, a payoff date is close, or tenants or an estate are involved.

Judge offers by what you net. Have the title company itemize the payoff, transfer fee, the $30 recording fee, prorated taxes and any repair credit. A listing that nets barely more than a clean cash offer may not be worth the wait.

Timing matters in a village with many rural lots, since a buyer who needs a loan will want an inspection of septic, drainage and permit records before closing. A cash buyer can skip some of that waiting, but the deed, transfer return, tax proration and condition report still apply, and your net figure should show all of them.

sections.h2: Steps to follow before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Call the Building Department for the permit history and close out any open work.
  2. Ask Racine County Planning and Development for septic records if the lot has a mound system.
  3. Check the assessor's page for your parcel's value and the current schedule.
  4. Prepare the condition report, or the vacant land report if the parcel has no buildings.
  5. Have the title company or an attorney draft the deed, then file the transfer return online.
  6. Record the deed with the Racine County Register of Deeds.

Doing the first four before you list shortens the time between an accepted offer and closing.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Caledonia house?
faqs.a: At the Racine County Register of Deeds, which charges a flat $30. File the Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return online with the Department of Revenue first.

faqs.q: What transfer fee applies to a Caledonia sale?
faqs.a: The state charges the seller 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22.

faqs.q: When can I appeal a Caledonia assessment?
faqs.a: Each year after notices are mailed, through open book and then the Board of Review. Ask the assessor's office for the dates, and file form PA-115A at least 48 hours before the first meeting.

faqs.q: Is a condition report required for a Caledonia sale?
faqs.a: Usually. Chapter 709 sets a 10-day deadline after the contract is accepted, and a late report lets the buyer rescind. Fiduciaries who never lived in the home are excused.
